nodes.name: PtNi/Ru@CFN synthesis
nodes.procedure: Details can be found in the Experiment Section (Figures S1-S7, Supporting Information).
nodes.source_text: experimentally, we alloyed Pt with Fe, Co, and Ni on the surface of Ru confined in the crystalline fullerene network (PtM/Ru@CFN), details can be found in the Experiment Section (Figures S1-S7, Supporting Information)

To deliver a current density of 10 mA cm^{-2}, specifically, it requires an overpotential (η10) of 25 mV for PtNi/Ru@CFN, much lower than that of Pt/Ru@CFN (58 mV), Ni/Ru@CFN (73 mV), Ru@CFN (45 mV) or the commercial Pt/C (36 mV). As displayed in Figure 4b, the corresponding Tafel slope for PtNi/Ru@CFN is also much lower... The Faradic efficiency of PtNi/Ru@CFN was measured as ca. 98% under 1.0 M KOH at 20 mA cm^{-2}... delivering robust current density of 10 mA cm^{-2} for at least 70 h... showing negligible decay of polarization curve after 2000 cycles of cycling voltammetry (CV)

the LSV curve of PtNi/Ru@CFN exhibits a superior electrocatalytic activity with a η10 of 29 mV and a Tafel slope of 37.08 mV dec^{-1}... The Faradic efficiency of PtNi/Ru@CFN was measured to be 98% under 0.5 M H2SO4 at 20 mA cm^{-2}

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns show diffraction peaks at 10.8°, 17.7° and 20.8° assigned to fcc C60, peaks attributed to crystallized PtNi alloy and hexagonal Ru structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 2a, besides the diffraction peaks (10.8°, 17.7° and 20.8°) assigned to the face-centered cubic (fcc) C60 (JCPDS No. 00-044-0558), the peaks attributed to crystallized PtNi alloy and hexagonal Ru structure can be similarly observed for the PtNi/Ru@CFN...

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra show distinct vibrational signals for C60 at 270, 430, 491, 711, 773 and 1465 cm^{-1} assigned to Hg(1), Hg(1), Ag(1), Hg(3), Hg(4) and Ag(2) modes respectively, with slight downshift of Ag(2) mode indicating charge transfer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the PtNi/Ru@CFN exhibits the distinct vibrational signals for C60, (i.e., 270, 430, 491, 711, 773 and 1465 cm^{-1} are assigned to the Hg(1), Hg(1), Ag(1), Hg(3), Hg(4) and Ag(2), respectively).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM image shows 3D nanoflower-like architecture of PtNi/Ru@CFN catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Typically, the PtNi/Ru@CFN catalyst is of a 3D nanoflower-like architecture according to its typical scanning electron microscopy (SEM) image (Figure 2c).

nodes.characterization_summary: AC-HAADF-STEM confirms crystallized PtNi alloy with lattice fringes of 0.189 nm (111) and 0.218 nm (200), Ru atom embedded in C60 (222) facets along (101) plane.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The characteristic lattice fringe distance of 0.189 nm attributed to the (111) plane and 0.218 nm ascribed to the (200) facets of PtNi (Figure 2e-h), while a Ru atom along the (101) crystal plane was embedded in the fullerene C60 (222) facets (Figure 2i-l).

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt 4f XPS shows metallic Pt 4f7/2 at 71.72 eV and 4f5/2 at 75.07 eV, surface oxidized Pt at 73.00 and 76.61 eV; Ru 3p shows metallic Ru at 461.81 and 484.18 eV, Ru^{x+} at 463.71 and 486.99 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the predominate metallic Pt 4f7/2 and 4f5/2 in the high-resolution XPS spectrum were observed at 71.72 and 75.07 eV (Figure 3a), respectively, while the peaks located at 73.00 and 76.61 eV were attributed to the surface oxidized Pt.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt and Ru K-edge XANES overlap with Pt foil and Ru foil indicating metallic Pt and Ru; Ni K-edge between Ni foil and NiO indicating surface oxidation of Ni.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From the X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectra displayed in Figure 3c-e, the Pt and Ru K-edge adsorption position are almost overlapped with Pt foil and Ru foil, demonstrating the predominant formation of metallic Pt and Ru, while the Ni K-edge is located between Ni foil and NiO...

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt K-edge shows Pt-Ni at 2.37 Å and Pt-Pt at 2.85 Å; Ru K-edge shows Ru-Ru at 2.43 Å and Ru-C at 1.78 Å; Ni K-edge shows Ni-Ni at 2.25 Å, Ni-Pt at 2.76 Å and Ni-O at 1.68 Å with CN of 3.9.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 3f, the main peak located at 2.37 Å and the shoulder peak at 2.85 Å in the Pt K-edge FT-EXAFS spectrum of PtNi/Ru@CFN are ascribed to the Pt-Ni and Pt-Pt bond, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: WT-EXAFS confirms formation of PtNi alloy anchored on metallic Ru substrate.
nodes.evidence_snippet: wavelet transform (WT) of the K-edge EXAFS spectra for PtNi/Ru@CFN (Figure 3i-k) further demonstrated the formation of PtNi alloy anchored on metallic Ru substrate.

nodes.characterization_summary: H2-TPD shows main desorption peak at 416°C for PtNi/Ru@CFN (vs 465°C for Ru@CFN) and additional peak at 277°C indicating stronger hydrogen desorption capability.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The main desorption peak of Ru@CFN was observed at 465°C, while the desorption peak for PtNi/Ru@CFN was extensively reduced to 416°C... another desorption peak for PtNi/Ru@CFN emerged at 277°C...

nodes.characterization_summary: CV in non-Faradaic region gives Cdl of 87.37 mF cm^{-2} (alkaline) and 38.39 mF cm^{-2} (acidic) for PtNi/Ru@CFN indicating enhanced ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure S21 (Supporting Information), the PtNi/Ru@CFN exhibits remarkably enhanced Cdl (87.37 mF cm^{-2})... The Cdl of PtNi/Ru@CFN was calculated to be 38.39 mF cm^{-2} (Figure S26, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows smaller charge transfer resistance Rct for PtNi/Ru@CFN indicated by smaller semicircle diameter.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the PtNi/Ru@CFN sample possesses a smaller semicircle diameter in the high-frequency region of the Nyquist plots compared to the control ones, suggesting its favorable charge transfer resistance (Rct).

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows Pt-OH* peaks at 1135 and 1530 cm^{-1}, Ru-H stretching at 875 cm^{-1} in alkaline; H-O-H bending at 1634 cm^{-1} in acid; O-H stretching modes deconvoluted into 4-HB·H2O, 2-HB·H2O, and free water.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The vibration peaks located at 1135 and 1530 cm^{-1} could be assigned to Pt-OH* in alkaline (Figure 5h)... and the hydrogen adsorption of Ru-H stretching vibration (vRu-H*) peak emerged at 875 cm^{-1}. Whereas in an acid condition, a rather weak H-O-H bending vibration (δO-H) appeared at 1634 cm^{-1} (Figure 5i).

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ ATR-IR shows water bending at 1654/1651 cm^{-1}, stretching at ~3225 cm^{-1}; Ru-H* at 2106 cm^{-1} (alkaline) and 2113 cm^{-1} (acid); Pt-OH* wagging at 1423/1420 cm^{-1}.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the peaks emerged at 1654 (1651) cm^{-1} and ≈3225 cm^{-1} were ascribed to the bending (δO-H) and stretching (vH-O-H) vibration mode of interfacial water... the signal at 2106 cm^{-1} (in alkaline) and 2113 cm^{-1} (in acid) can be attributed to the interaction of adsorbed hydrogen with Ru (vRu-H*)... the wagging mode of Pt-OH* vibration (δPt-OH*) in PtNi/Ru@CFN was observed both in 1 M KOH (1423 cm^{-1}) and 0.5 M H2SO4 (1420 cm^{-1}) media.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ EQCM shows mass increment during H adsorption and decrement during desorption (0.25-0.52 V vs RHE); Δm/dq of 1.46 and 1.57 g/mol electrons for adsorption/desorption.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The result revealed a mass increment during the hydrogen adsorption process and a decrement during desorption in the potential range of 0.25-0.52 V versus reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE). By plotting the mass change response against the corresponding charge consumption, Δm/dq (mass change per electron) of 1.46 and 1.57 g per mol electrons for the adsorption and desorption was obtained.
